chunks: When (Abraham) saw the moon rise, he said: "This is my Lord." But when it set, he said: "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among those who go astray."

key_terms.الضَّالِّينَ: The astray / those who go wrong

ai.seo_question: What does Abraham mean when he says 'This is my Lord' regarding the moon?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as Abraham's methodical progression through monotheistic stages (marjiyyah), moving from the moon to the sun to the stars, thereby refuting the idolaters' logic by demonstrating the impermanence of celestial bodies. The phrase 'This is my Lord' is understood not as a declaration of divinity for the moon itself, but as a rhetorical device to show that if the moon were the lord, its setting would constitute its death or disappearance, proving its inadequacy. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on using rational deduction (aql) to arrive at tawhid, serving as a foundational model for intellectual faith before prophetic revelation.
